invariants.title: Instance identity is immutable and canonical
invariants.rule: instance_id is immutable identity, must be a canonical non-empty GUID before path construction or durable association, and friendly names are presentation only.

invariants.title: Registry is authoritative once active
invariants.rule: Once a valid multi-Hub registry is active, Hub selection and lifecycle routing derive from the registry/active selection rather than legacy single-instance inference.

invariants.title: Instance-bound artifacts validate instance identity
invariants.rule: Any instance-bound CURRENT, checkpoint, transport or lifecycle artifact must validate its instance_id against the intended registered instance before use or commit.

invariants.title: Cross-instance application fails closed
invariants.rule: No Hub package, CURRENT, checkpoint, exchange payload or lifecycle mutation may be applied to a different instance than the captured intended instance.

invariants.title: Switching changes selection only
invariants.rule: Switching the active Hub never moves, clones or rewrites Hub bytes; it changes authoritative active selection and compatibility shadow only after target validation.

invariants.title: Rebinding repairs a registered path without changing identity
invariants.rule: Rebinding an existing instance to a new vault path preserves the immutable instance_id, freshly validates that the requested Hub has that exact identity and an activation-eligible CURRENT, updates the registry path atomically, and never moves or clones Hub bytes.

invariants.title: Manager update state is global
invariants.rule: Manager updates and Manager-global state remain global; multi-Hub routing must not accidentally instance-scope Manager update packages or product installation.

invariants.title: Hub lifecycle state is per instance
invariants.rule: Hub inbox, CURRENT, checkpoints and rollback history are owned by the intended instance once registry mode is active.

invariants.title: Older Manager compatibility never cross-pairs Hub state
invariants.rule: Compatibility shadowing for older Managers must never pair one Hub vault with another Hub's CURRENT/checkpoint, including during switch and post-commit recovery.

invariants.title: Hub-mutating operations use captured invocation context
invariants.rule: Every Hub-mutating operation is bound either to a captured immutable instance_id or to an explicitly captured single-instance expectation, and that expectation is freshly revalidated at the transaction boundary.

invariants.title: Authoritative commits use fresh activation-eligible state
invariants.rule: Immediately before an authoritative registry/active commit, the exact staged Hub/CURRENT pair and relevant target identity must be freshly validated as activation-eligible.

invariants.title: Durable commit and post-commit verification are distinct
invariants.rule: If durable state committed but subsequent verification failed, committed state is preserved and the result explicitly reports durable commit success versus ambiguous commit status versus definite pre-commit failure.

invariants.title: Filesystem publication fails closed on occupied destination
invariants.rule: Validated staged Hub/state directories are published with fail-if-destination-exists semantics; an externally-created destination cannot change publication meaning.

invariants.title: Windows paths and IDs are normalized before comparison/construction
invariants.rule: Equivalent Windows paths are compared with Windows-appropriate case semantics and untrusted instance IDs are validated before use in repository/state-relative paths.

invariants.title: Cancellation, success and partial failure are distinct
invariants.rule: Nested/interactive lifecycle actions must distinguish clean cancellation, successful materialization and partial/invalid materialization; downstream commits may proceed only after explicit success.

invariants.title: Compatibility entry points preserve canonical safety contracts
invariants.rule: Documented aliases, old-entry compatibility commands and self-update restart handoffs must preserve the same Hub-context, validation and fail-closed invariants as the canonical frontend/runtime path.

invariants.title: Instance-owned discovery is independent of unrelated global state
invariants.rule: After registry activation, discovery of instance-owned Hub inputs/state must not depend on the existence or health of unrelated Manager-global inbox/state paths.

invariants.title: Recovery does not depend on health of replaced state
invariants.rule: A recovery action must not require successful validation of the broken active state it is explicitly intended to bypass, replace or rebind; it validates the requested recovery target instead.

invariants.title: Registry activation preserves pending Hub-input reachability
invariants.rule: Activating multi-Hub registry must not silently make previously reachable valid Hub APPROVED, CANDIDATE or candidate-transport inputs unreachable; initialization must migrate, explicitly reject or fail closed before activation.
